[done] Native lldb backend shipped end-to-end and verified against a REAL live lldb (fetched via nixpkgs for this session; not yet in flake.nix devShell — see Open Owner-Q). Codegen: TStmt::LineMarker + emit_bundle_dbg/compile_for_debug emit `// jet:line N` markers gated by cx.debug_linemap (off by default — zero effect on normal builds, golden tests, or the JIT tier; confirmed via full test suite + `cargo test --workspace` diffing). New Source/Debug/{LineMap,Inferior,Native,Dap}.rs. `jet debug` auto-dispatches interpreter vs native via the SAME E2203 boundary scan (needs_native) — one command, one meaning (I8); `--dap` forces native for editor launch; `--raw-frames` (D-DBG2) shows raw Rust file:line. Reuses the exact ratified (jet) vocabulary (D-DBG3) over both backends. Live-lldb verification surfaced and fixed THREE real bugs a docs-only implementation would have shipped broken: (1) lldb never re-prints a bare prompt over a pipe (echoes command instead) — naive prompt-wait hangs forever, fixed with a sentinel-command read loop; (2) a resume command's own stop banner is asynchronous and can lose a race to the NEXT command's reply — fixed by always deriving position from a synchronous follow-up `bt`, never the resume's own text; (3) the debuggee inherits lldb's stdout by default, so a Jet `print()` can tear a control-channel sentinel in half — fixed by redirecting debuggee stdout/stderr to temp files via `settings set target.output/error-path` and draining them into the transcript. Also loads rustc's own Rust pretty-printer (lldb_lookup.py + lldb_commands, same two files rust-lldb loads) so String/&str locals render as `"text"` instead of raw allocator internals. Tests: 12 new unit tests (LineMap/Inferior, no lldb needed) + tests/debug_native.rs (5 tests, gated on lldb presence like tests/observe.rs gates on rustc — skips clean without it). New example examples/features/189_debug_native.jet (native-only via `use core.fs`) + golden .out. cards.title: Full HTTP core library — client + server (D-NETDEP1=A, owner-expanded mandate)
cards.body: Owner mandate (2026-06-26, expanding D-NETDEP1=A): Jet ships a full, complete HTTP library — both client AND server — as a core library, better than Go's net/http. D-NETDEP1's approved pure-Rust crate (ureq/minreq) is only the BOOTSTRAP backing c157's build-time fetch(url, sha256:); the native-ize end-state (Epoch-3 dep rule) is a first-party Jet/Rust HTTP stdlib. SCOPE: client (request/response, methods, headers, body, streaming, TLS, redirects, timeouts) + server (listener, router, handler, middleware, request/response types, graceful shutdown). The client+server API surface (naming + shapes) is SYNTAX/stdlib-surface design needing its own decision docs + ballots BEFORE code — drive from a real-world example per owner-anti-repetition + owner-decision-doc-style. NOT this card: c157's fetch backend (ships first against the bootstrap crate).
cards.plan:
Full HTTP core library — client + server (D-NETDEP1=A mandate; D-HTTPLIB1=A function-first mux; D-HTTPLIB2=B split client/server; D-HTTPLIB3=C HTTP/1.1+HTTP/2+WebSocket; D-HTTPLIB4=B rustls TLS — all ratified & in canon). Bootstrap crates (ureq/hyper, tungstenite, rustls/webpki-roots) wired via the stdlib FFI-bridge pattern (emit bridge template text; never add to the jet compiler Cargo.toml; I6 holds — never in Source/). Native-ize end-state: first-party Jet/Rust HTTP stack.
Staged build: (1) core.http.client — Request/Response, methods, headers, body, streaming, redirects, timeouts, rustls TLS; this also provides the backend for c157's comptime `fetch(url, sha256:)` (record {url,sha256} in .jet/lock) — ship first to unblock c157. (2) core.http.server — listener, function-first `mux` (mux.get/post(path, fn(req:Request)->Response)), `req.params["id"]`, middleware, graceful shutdown. (3) HTTP/2 + WebSocket upgrade. Each stage: examples + goldens; no I4 diagnostics unless misuse surfaces. Big multi-PR track — sequence client before server.

cards.title: Ignore secondary return values / discard errors (Jai-style `content, ok := f()`)
cards.body: Ideas.md (scratch L20 + Level-3): allow discarding secondary results or an error like Jai — `content := read_entire_file(...)` ignoring the error, or `content, ok := ...` to capture it. Jet today uses `T ? E` and treats ignored fallible results as errors/test-only. Bundle-risk: multiple-returns and ignored-errors are distinct.
cards.plan: D-IGNORERET2=A implementation plan: (1) register `#Suppress(MustUse)` marker and `.drop("reason")` terminal method in Syntax.rs; (2) parser accepts marker on block/fn and method-chain terminal call; (3) sema recognizes `.drop` only on `#MustUse`/fallible values, requires non-empty string literal reason, and emits a lint rather than hard error; (4) `#Suppress(MustUse)` suppresses within lexical body and records an audit warning; (5) codegen erases discarded value after evaluating side effects; (6) diagnostics + ui snapshots for missing reason, unsupported receiver, and accidental ignore; (7) examples/goldens.

cards.title: Crypto/secrets push: misuse-resistant envelopes, agility, TTL/rotting secrets
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 crypto/secrets push. Merges post-quantum agility (#71) and TTL/rotting secrets (#59) into misuse-resistant crypto envelopes. This card owns safe high-level crypto APIs and secret lifetime controls.
cards.plan:
Canonical crypto/secrets implementation plan. Default API must be misuse-resistant; raw primitives stay expert-only.

Build order:
1. Preserve/finish RNG split prerequisite: deterministic PRNG and CSPRNG remain structurally separate.
2. Envelope API: crypto.seal/open and crypto.sign/verify hide nonce/mode/key details; versioned envelope metadata; clear error types; no raw AES/ChaCha/RSA beginner path.
3. Algorithm agility: design hybrid-ready envelope metadata and algorithm ids now; do not expose PQ primitive until backend exists; migration tests prove old envelopes still open.
4. TTL/rotting secrets: core.time.Expiring<T> and core.secrets.Rotting<T>; constructors require clock/context and deadline/ttl; access returns T? or fallible expired error.
5. Static/lint support: warn/error for expired unwrap in test-known clock cases; reject crypto API misuse that bypasses envelope surface.

Acceptance: examples for seal/open, sign/verify, envelope version migration, expiring cache, rotating secret; golden tests; ui snapshots for wrong RNG/raw primitive misuse/expired unchecked access; docs explain expert escape hatches.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: build-cache normalization model — complete action identity owned by #419
cards.body: Prior cache-key contract is insufficient for imported/generated inputs, dependencies, targets, toolchains, policy, and observable source. E4-JP2 replaces it.
cards.plan: docs/plans/epoch-4/cas-build-cache.md

log.text: 2026-07-09 truth audit: reclassified from shipped capability to historical substrate; world-class milestone owns live completion.

Independently re-verified with EXTRA scrutiny (orchestrator) given this card touches the core compile pipeline (I2/I3): nix develop -c cargo build --workspace clean. Targeted tests confirmed exactly: tests/build_cache_normalization.rs 10/10 (whitespace/comment/rename/reorder/profile/version-sensitive + 4 extra discrimination guards), tests/build_cache_race.rs 1/1 (8-concurrent-process integrity check), crates/jet-foundation lib CanonicalAST:: 3/3.

Went beyond targeted tests given the risk here — manual end-to-end smoke of the real jet binary, not just the test suite: (1) nix develop -c ./target/debug/jet run hello.jet twice — first run showed the front-end effects summary, SECOND run (cache hit) correctly skipped it and still printed "hello, world" — confirms the short-circuit works for real, not just in unit tests. (2) edited the source (changed the printed string) and re-ran — correctly re-ran the full pipeline (front-end summary reappeared) and printed the NEW string, confirming edit/rename-sensitivity holds in practice. (3) jet build produced a working binary. (4) manually reproduced the exact race scenario from the plan: 3 concurrent jet run processes, all named main.jet in different directories with different content, launched simultaneously via nix develop's shell — each process's stdout correctly matched its own source with zero cross-contamination, confirming the cache-poisoning race fix holds under a real concurrent run, not just the automated 8-process regression test.

Full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace run to completion, exit code 0, zero FAILED/error lines. The I2/I3 soundness argument (cache hit = replay of a previously-validated exact whole-program AST + toolchain version + manifest bytes + profile, never a validation bypass; embed_file/embed_bytes correctly declines caching rather than risk external-state staleness) was reviewed and holds — no gap found on the orchestrator's independent read either. This was the last card in the owner's stated jetpack sequence for this session (#99 -> #176 -> #90 -> #3 -> #13 -> #179 -> #85). Closing: phase -> done.

E4 prep: plan expanded, zero ballots. Located real cache-poisoning race (CmdCompile.rs build(): rustc -o onto shared build/<stem> before store_cached copy — concurrent same-stem processes cross-contaminate) + fix (per-process temp path, atomic rename). D-BUILDNORM1=A ratified but cache_key hashes post-codegen Rust today, defeating incremental point — plan moves key to pre-sema canonical AST bytes + toolchain salt. Hash naming interlocked with #3 envelope.

Interlock noted 2026-07-02: D-JPK-CACHE1=A freezes cache-envelope fields (output hash, platform key, signature slot, provenance link) into the hangar/lock schema — normalization contract must carry them.
D-BUILDNORM1=A recorded and implementation plan attached. Advanced to ready.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

[epoch restructure 2026-06-26] - → e5. Owner restructure: E3 = every major feature; E4 = Jai metaprogramming; E5 = jetpack/jetos; E6 = CI & documentation (deferred until features are set).

Found and reproduced a real cache-poisoning race in the current build cache (Source/BuildCache.rs + Source/CmdCompile.rs build()): cache_key() correctly SHA256-hashes the generated rust_code+profile, but the binary is compiled to a SHARED non-unique path (bin_path(file), e.g. build/main, keyed by source stem only) BEFORE store_cached(key, &bin) copies it into the content-addressed slot. Two jet processes compiling different sources with the same stem concurrently (e.g. two run/test invocations both producing build/main) can race: process A computes hash_A from its own rust_code, but by the time it calls store_cached, process B has already overwritten build/main with its binary, so hash_A permanently maps to B's binary in the shared ~/.cache/jet/build/ cache. Repro: many concurrent/rapid jet run invocations during Epoch 3 syntax-wave work; tests/cli.rs simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest started failing (build/main.rs correct, cached binary under the correct hash printed wrong output). Fix for this card: compile to a unique per-process temp path before the content-addressed copy, so store_cached never races on a shared path. Cleared ~/.cache/jet/build/ as an immediate workaround; the poisoning will recur without the root-cause fix.

Implemented both parts.

PART 1 (race fix, section 0): BuildCache::store_cached (Source/BuildCache.rs) is now atomic -- writes to dir/bin.tmp.<pid> then fs::rename into dir/bin. CmdCompile.rs::build() no longer compiles onto the shared build/<stem> path directly: it now allocates a private per-process working dir build/.work.<bin_name>.<pid>/ holding the generated .rs, the rustc output binary, AND (discovered while writing the regression test) rustc's own crate-name-derived intermediate .rcgu.o object files, which also collided across concurrent same-stem builds and are now isolated the same way (rustc invoked with an explicit --crate-name pinned to the file stem, since the private .rs filename is not a valid crate identifier). store_cached is called against the private binary (safe: only races other processes computing the identical content-addressed key), then the private binary is fs::rename'd onto the shared build/<stem> display path (last-writer-wins on that convenience path is fine; it was never a content identity). Regression test tests/build_cache_race.rs::concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache spawns 8 concurrent jet-run processes on distinct main.jet sources (different literal output) sharing a cwd and a JET_CACHE_DIR, then re-runs each source from its own isolated cwd against the same cache and asserts each cache hit returns exactly that source's own binary. This reproduces and pins the exact scenario the plan described (previously broke tests/cli.rs::simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest under concurrent Epoch 3 work) and fails without the fix (verified: reproduced the crate-name and .rcgu.o collisions live before fixing them).

PART 2 (normalization, sections 1-3, D-BUILDNORM1=A): new crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs -- canonical_bytes(bundle: &ProgramBundle) serializes the WHOLE pre-sema bundle (entry file plus every module the loader resolved via imports, not just the entry) using each module's Debug-derived rendering of (pub_file, web_target_ceiling, html_path, imports, items) with a custom strip_spans() pass that removes every 'Span { start: N, end: M }' substring while leaving string/char literal contents (including ones that text-mimic a Span rendering) untouched -- verified by a dedicated unit test. Confirmed via recon (subagent read of AST.rs) that NO AST node stores comments or doc-comments (parser drops them entirely), so whitespace/comment insensitivity falls out for free from parsing + span-stripping; confirmed no HashMap/HashSet appears anywhere in the serialized item/import subtree (only in bundle-level resolved-state fields deliberately excluded, e.g. used_core/import_targets/web_partitions/dep_roots), so Debug rendering is deterministic. ast_cache_key(bundle, profile_tag, jet_version) = SHA256(canonical_bytes + 0 + profile_tag + 0 + jet_version) -- SHA-256 via the existing SHA256::sha256_hex, matching Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash's algorithm (D-JPK-CACHE1=A interlock: same mechanism, not wired together yet, deferred to Epoch 6 as the plan directs). CanonicalAST re-exported through the full seam chain (jet-foundation -> jet-lexer/jet-parser -> jet-sema -> jet-codegen -> jet-driver -> Source/lib.rs) so Source/CmdCompile.rs can call jet::CanonicalAST::ast_cache_key.

CmdCompile.rs: new native_cache_key(file, profile_tag, mode_tag) loads the program pre-sema via Loader::load_entry_with_overlay (confirmed via recon this runs lex+parse+import-resolution only, no Sema::check_bundle), returns None (never cache) if any module's source contains embed_file/embed_bytes (external-file-bytes-not-in-AST gap, closed conservatively rather than papered over) or if the file fails to parse; folds in a SHA-256 of the enclosing pkg.jet's raw bytes (manifest_fingerprint) plus Manifest::COMPILER_VERSION as the toolchain/policy salt, so an effect-budget (D-EFFBUDGET1) tightening in pkg.jet or a compiler version bump invalidates old entries rather than being masked by an unchanged AST. jet run (mode_tag=='run', no --emit-rust) now short-circuits the ENTIRE front end on a cache hit -- sema and codegen never run, only the pre-sema parse inside the key computation -- and directly execs the cached binary. jet build deliberately keeps running its full front end even on a cache hit (only rustc is skipped, as before) because tests/pkg.rs asserts the unconditional per-build 'effects:' stderr summary and the capability summary on jet build stdout; confirmed via recon no jet-run test snapshots that stderr line, so the deeper run-side short-circuit is test-safe. jet test/doctest/bench/dev/debug builds keep their existing cache behavior (test gets its own mode_tag-scoped AST key so a test-harness binary can never be served for jet run; dev/doctest/bench/debug pass cache_key=None -- interactive/one-shot, still race-safe via build()'s private workdir). The old BuildCache::cache_key(source, profile_tag) signature is untouched and still used by BuildCache.rs's own unit tests; nothing else referenced it (checked via grep) so no call site needed updating.

SOUNDNESS ARGUMENT (I2/I3), verified end to end: a cache hit means (a) this exact whole-program AST -- entry plus every imported module, span/comment-stripped, identifier/order-sensitive -- (b) under this exact toolchain version and (c) this exact pkg.jet manifest bytes and (d) this exact build profile, was already parsed, type-checked, codegen'd, rustc-compiled to success, and (for jet run) executed at least once before. Skipping sema+codegen on a hit therefore replays a previously-validated result; it can never let unchecked code through, because storage only happens after a full successful pipeline run, and any input that could change sema's outcome for byte-identical AST bytes (imports -- closed by whole-bundle hashing; toolchain/codegen version -- closed by the version salt; manifest-driven policy like effect budgets -- closed by the manifest-fingerprint salt; embedded external file bytes -- closed by unconditionally declining to cache embed_file/embed_bytes programs) is either folded into the AST, folded into the salt, or excluded from caching outright. No gap found that required stopping; the one real external-state hazard (embed_file/embed_bytes) is handled by declining to cache rather than by hashing file bytes into the key, since Sema's own comptime_inputs tracking is only available post-sema and re-deriving it pre-sema was unnecessary when simple exclusion is sound and cheap.

TESTS: crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (3: strip_spans_removes_span_renderings, strip_spans_keeps_span_lookalike_inside_string_literal, strip_spans_keeps_char_literal_with_quote); tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (10: whitespace_insensitive, comment_insensitive, rename_sensitive, reorder_sensitive, profile_sensitive, version_sensitive, operator_sensitive, literal_sensitive, string_literal_content_sensitive, stable_across_reloads -- covers all six named properties plus extra discrimination guards); tests/build_cache_race.rs (1: concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache, 8 concurrent processes). All new tests green; smoke-verified manually outside the suite too (jet run cache-miss then cache-hit shows front-end skip via -v; jet build cache-hit still prints its effects/capabilities summary).

FULL SUITE: nix develop -c cargo test --no-fail-fast run twice independently, exit 0 both times, 70/70 test binaries 'test result: ok', 0 FAILED, 1058 individual tests passed total (a one-off engine_dispatch::json_flag_forwarded_verbatim_to_engine failure on an earlier concurrent run reproduced as a PATH/binary-copy flake under full-suite parallelism -- passed alone and on both full clean reruns, unrelated to this card's files).

EXIT CRITERIA: all checked -- race fixed (store_cached atomic + build() private workdir + rename-publish); key is pre-sema canonical AST, not post-codegen Rust, with sema/codegen skipped entirely on a jet-run hit; toolchain-version salt folded in; all six normalization properties tested and passing; naming/algorithm (SHA-256, output_hash-shaped) consistent with D-JPK-CACHE1's Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash; full suite green including the new concurrent-process regression test.

Files touched: Source/BuildCache.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, Source/CmdDevTools.rs (two build() call sites updated for the new cache_key param), crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs (new), crates/jet-foundation/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-lexer/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-driver/src/lib.rs, Source/lib.rs (re-export chain), tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (new), tests/build_cache_race.rs (new).

cards.title: Core library breadth push: DB drivers, YAML, Unicode text, compression, linalg
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 Core library breadth push. Merges YAML (#16), Unicode text (#66), compression codecs (#67), and linalg/math (#70) into the general DB/Core library interface card. This card owns library breadth that makes Jet a daily-driver TS/Swift replacement without new core-language mechanisms.
cards.plan:
Canonical Core library breadth plan. Prefer stdlib/library APIs over language features; compiler changes only for checked builtin namespaces/types already approved.

Build order:
1. General DB/sql driver interface: parameterized-only query API, no string interpolation SQL, driver trait/interface, transaction hooks, tests with safe stub/sqlite path as available.
2. Data formats: finish YAML 1.2 advanced tags/features under core.encoding.yaml; keep JSON/TOML/CSV behavior stable.
3. Unicode text: opt-in core.text.unicode package for grapheme iteration and normalization; plain String remains one type; docs warn about byte/scalar/grapheme distinctions.
4. Compression codecs: gzip/zstd/brotli under core.compress; archive module remains archive-specific; streaming APIs where possible.
5. Linalg/math: vectors, matrices, decompositions, FFT/SIMD fallback; no operator overload outside already-ratified math family.

Acceptance: one example per module with expected output; golden tests; API docs/reference updates; misuse diagnostics where API is safety-critical (SQL parameters, invalid Unicode form, malformed compressed stream); pay-for-what-you-call codegen remains R10.

log.text: Reopened because the Core-breadth umbrella includes Unicode and streaming/library claims that remain subset implementations. Detailed repair lives on #298 and domain cards.

(1) D-DBDRIVER1: core.db reworked to `DbConnection`/`DbValue`/`DbError` types, `.query/.query_one/.execute` take SQL + a separate `[DbValue]` bind list (never string-spliced), old raw `exec(sql)`/`query_json(sql)` escape removed entirely; `.begin/.commit/.rollback` transaction hooks (explicit methods, not `#Transact` reuse — that mechanism is generic value-snapshot rollback, not SQL transactions, confirmed by reading tests/rollback.rs; wiring it in would need new unratified semantics). Example 128 rewritten: proves an injection-looking bind value round-trips as inert data and a rolled-back insert doesn't stick. (4) D-CODECS1: new core.compress.gzip/core.compress.zstd modules (own FFI-bridge plumbing, Compress.rs), decompress is fallible (Result), unlike core.archive's silent-empty-on-corrupt gzip. Whole-buffer compress/decompress only — streaming Reader/Writer and leveled-compress correctly descoped: JetFileReader/JetFileWriter are concrete structs, no generic Reader/Writer trait exists yet to build a streaming codec wrapper on. Examples 187/188. Full `nix develop -c cargo test` green (all binaries, 0 failed), zero new Cargo.toml deps in any crates/* crate (rusqlite/flate2/zstd stay FFI.rs string literals per I6). syntax-decisions.md D-CODECS1/D-DBDRIVER1 updated from 'not yet implemented' to implemented.

cards.title: JIT tier-1a: Cranelift JIT (dev-loop hot-reload) — c139
cards.body: Ideas.md: add Cranelift JIT, later own bytecode/native JIT. Was Tower c139 (ready); c140/c141 (own bytecode VM / own native JIT) are separate frozen v2 cards. Jet is AOT-compiled; the Cranelift JIT is the optional hot-reload dev accelerator (tier-1 over interpreter tier-0), not how the language runs. Accepted work. Bundle-risk: Cranelift JIT vs later custom tiers differ. Owner requirement (2026-06-30): JIT and `jet run` must be functionally identical on every program the AOT path covers; native stays the performance tier. `jit_covers` must converge on `tir_covers`, not fall back to the E2201 interpreter for tasks/channels/Core.
cards.plan: JIT/AOT parity by construction. Canonical plan: docs/plans/epoch-3/jit-aot-parity.md. Orchestration: implementation agent must first read .agents/prompts/OrchestrationPrompt.md and run as that orchestrator. Owner direction 2026-07-06: Jet wins two fronts. AOT targets C/C++/Rust/Go/Zig/Odin territory with optimized native binaries and expert control; JIT/dev targets JS/TS/Python/data-analysis/web-dev loops with rapid design/test/refine. Every AOT-runnable program must run under jet dev in some backend path with identical stdout/stderr/exit/diagnostics/panics/side effects. Native JIT lowering is preferred for speed; transparent shared-runtime/platform/AOT-subprocess fallback is valid when resident JIT hosting is unsafe or incomplete. User never owns backend gaps. cards.title: Concurrency runtime push: Go-scale M:N tasks + structured combinators
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 concurrency push. Merges #36 (Verse-style race/all/any/select combinators) and #103 (try-both / keep-the-winner) into the Go-scale M:N runtime card. Prior foundations already shipped: #102 taskgroup scope, #101 task-handle coroutine-grade controls, #112 deadline propagation. This card now owns the remaining runtime-quality push: native OS parking, structured combinator completion, select integration, cancellation correctness, observability, and scale/perf proof. No @async/await or function coloring; ordinary Jet code parks at wait/IO points under the task/channel/taskgroup model.
cards.plan:
Canonical concurrency implementation plan (D-ASYNCRT1=A, D-MNIO1=A, D-CONCCOMB1=A, D-RACEWIN1=A, D-CONCSELECT1=A). Build one model only: task/channel/taskgroup. No @async/await, no user coroutine primitive, no second race/select mechanism.

Already shipped foundations to preserve:
- #102: taskgroup g { ... }, g.task { ... }, wait/join, scope-exit ownership, existing g.all/g.race/g.any vertical slice.
- #101: task handles expose coroutine-grade controls (pause/resume/cancel/trace); coroutine substrate stays internal.
- #112: #Context(deadline:) flows through taskgroups and wait points; E3003 owns deadline diagnostics.
- #126 M1/M2: current scheduler vertical slice, channels/timers/yield hook, 160_scheduler_spawn.

Implementation order for dumb agents:
1. Inventory current behavior first. Read docs/spec/philosophy.md, syntax-decisions.md entries for D-ASYNCRT1/D-MNIO1/D-NURSERY1/D-TASKSCOPE1/D-CONCCOMB1/D-RACEWIN1/D-CONCSELECT1/D-DEADLINE1/D-COROUTINE1, docs/plans/epoch-3/concurrency-vision.md, Source/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, Source/Interpreter.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, task/channel sema/codegen, and tests for examples 131, 157, 158, 160.
2. Write missing acceptance tests before code. Add/extend examples/features concurrency examples plus CLI/golden tests for: 100k idle parked tasks or smallest CI-safe equivalent with a scale benchmark guard; channel receive wakes one parked task without busy-wait; taskgroup scope cancels losing race tasks; g.all fail-fast cancels siblings; g.race returns first success and cancels losers; g.any returns first completion including errors; if g.select() arms deregister losers; deadline firing wakes parked I/O/channel/task waits with Jet-owned E3003; detached tasks require explicit expert policy/name.
3. Replace cooperative-only scheduler gaps with real parker abstraction. Define internal runtime traits, not user syntax: Scheduler, Parker, TimerWheel, IoParker. Start with portable readiness fallback for tests; implement D-MNIO1 native backends behind cfg modules (Linux epoll/io_uring path, macOS/BSD kqueue, Windows IOCP). No external runtime dependency unless owner approves a new dep card.
4. Route every blocking-looking stdlib wait through the parker. Channel recv/send, timers/sleep, task join/wait, TCP accept/read/write, HTTP client/server waits must park Jet tasks, not OS threads. Real OS-blocking fallback must run on an explicit blocking pool and be observable; never silently block scheduler workers.
5. Finish structured combinators in taskgroup only. g.all/g.race/g.any/select are methods or scoped operations on the taskgroup; they create no detached work and return/propagate through one cancellation model. Implement D-RACEWIN1 inside g.race; #103 is merged here. Implement D-CONCCOMB1 here; #36 is merged here.
6. Implement D-CONCSELECT1 exactly as ratified: if-fused select over g.select() arms. Parser/sema/codegen/tests must reuse match/if-arm typing where possible. Select must register arms under taskgroup ownership, wake exactly one winner, deregister losers, and compose with deadlines/cancellation.
7. Add observability and misuse diagnostics. Runtime metrics: runnable/parked task counts, poller wake count, worker utilization, queue depth, cancelled losers. Diagnostics/lints: forgotten task handle wait, swallowed cancellation, deadline ignored, detached task without policy/name, real blocking call on scheduler worker.
8. Prove parity and scale. cargo test green; examples 131/157/158/160 still pass; add deterministic scheduler tests with fake clock; add stress tests gated for CI budget; add a benchmark/report target that demonstrates 100k parked connections/tasks when run locally. rustc errors remain ICE-only; all user errors are sema/driver diagnostics.

Exit criteria:
- One coherent public model in docs/spec/spec.md and examples: task/channel/taskgroup + scoped combinators + deadline context.
- No @async/await surface, no function coloring, no separate user coroutine API.
- Native parker path exists per platform or has named cfg-tested fallback with honest diagnostic/metric.
- race/all/any/select cannot leak losing tasks past taskgroup scope.
- CI-safe tests prove cancellation/deadline/wake correctness; local stress target proves 100k parked tasks/connections target.
- docs/plans/epoch-3/async-networking.md and concurrency-vision.md match implementation.

cards.title: Derive output mechanism (emit source fragments re-entering lexer/parser/sema) — D-METADERIVE1

cards.plan: D-METADERIVE1=A: implement user derive output as source fragments. Steps: (1) parser for `derive Trait for T { ... }`; (2) sema registers derive providers and enforces local-only orphan rule (trait or type local); (3) derive body runs at comptime with `T.reflect()` and `$name` splices; (4) emitted Jet text re-enters lexer/parser/sema per R11/D-CTCODEGEN1, never injects pre-parsed AST; (5) diagnostics for generated-fragment failure pin at the user `#[Trait]` trigger with optional generated context; (6) examples and goldens for a custom derive; (7) follow-up card for emit-template quoting, not a blocker.

Phase 8 done + committed, full suite green — CARD COMPLETE. D-STYLEUNIT1=A slice done + committed, full suite green: 10px/20px unit-family style lengths live; interim Length struct deleted; TIR distinct-field ICE fixed at class level (subset field/payload coverage + JetDebug for distinct). Card moves to DECIDING — all remaining work owner-gated: D-STYLEUNIT1 (open), new D-UIDEVSHELL1 (Phase 8 toolkit deps), new D-OSTARGET2 (ungated dispatch to OS-gated impls). Pre-existing bugs noted, untouched: #PubFile formatter reorder breaks idempotence; Type.{} zero-field construction E0119.

Raised D-STYLEUNIT1 (style length spelling — unit-family literal vs Length struct; Phase 3 shipped plain struct, unit-family attempt hit TIR subset-coverage ICE, see ballot). NOTE: prior handoff claiming D-UITREE1/D-STYLESHAPE1/D-MOTIONTIME1/D-A11YGATE1 open was STALE — all 4 ratified 2026-06-30, Phases 2-6 built with examples on disk. Remaining real work: Phase 9 (9.1/9.2 doc-comment rewording + syntax-decisions rows + fmt stability tests; 9.3 D-OSTARGET1 OS gating), Phase 8 behind devShell toolkit gate.

[handoff] Phases 1+7 verified DONE this session (see prior log entry for detail). Remaining scope, unchanged: Phase 2 (view model layer) blocked on open D-UITREE1; Phase 3 (typed styles) blocked on open D-STYLESHAPE1/D-STYLEUNIT1; Phase 4 (component kit) depends on 2+3; Phase 5 (motion) blocked on open D-MOTIONTIME1; Phase 6 (a11y) blocked on open D-A11YGATE1; Phase 8 (native OS backends) needs Phase 9.3 first; Phase 9 (D-WEBDEFAULT1/D-HTMLPAIR1 doc-comment rewording to 'ratified' + syntax-decisions.md rows, D-OSTARGET1 OS-target-gating implementation) is separately scoped, substantial, unbuilt work — see reactive-ui-stack.md §9 for the full spec, it's detailed and ready to implement (D-OSTARGET1=A ratified, no open gate). NEXT STEP if resuming this card: either raise the 4 open decisions (D-UITREE1/D-STYLESHAPE1/D-MOTIONTIME1/D-A11YGATE1) as ballots if not already ballot-ready, or start Phase 9 (fully unblocked, no open decision) as the next concrete chunk of work.

Phase 1 (computed alias) + Phase 7 (web/DOM backend) verified 100% already-shipped, not stubs — confirmed via targeted tests: web_build (13/13), web_dev (3/3), corelib core_module_items_covers_known_core_modules, tir reactive_scope_marker, plus a manual native+web dual-run of examples/features/web/ui_web_reactive.jet through real node, byte-identical output. Reworded the stale plan doc to match. Remaining scope: Phases 2/3/5/6 gated on open decisions (D-UITREE1, D-STYLESHAPE1, D-MOTIONTIME1, D-A11YGATE1), Phase 4 depends on 2+3, Phase 8 (native OS backends) and Phase 9 (web-target ballot batch: D-WEBDEFAULT1/D-HTMLPAIR1/D-OSTARGET1 cleanup) still open — card stays building, not done.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

D-HTMLPAIR1 amended: added option B (manifest target field, composed with #Html file marker + precedence chain). D-OSTARGET1/D-WEBDEFAULT1 reviewed under the magic/expert/audit lens: sound as written, no change.

devserver ergonomics (owner feedback): (1) devserver.app() — new zero-arg constructor meaning watch the file jet dev launched; run_dev_entry passes the canonical absolute path to the compiled dev() program via JET_DEV_FILE, so no path literal is needed at all and it works from any invocation directory (kills the prior repo-root-only caveat). Clear error if the binary is run outside jet dev. (2) for_app(path) now canonicalizes relative-or-absolute against invocation cwd up front. (3) .html(path) already resolved against the app files dir (matches #Html semantics); absolute paths pass through via Path::join. (4) Real bug found during foreign-cwd verification: DevServer shelled out to bare jet from PATH — wrong version risk generally, and the nix devshells cwd-sensitive jet wrapper broke outright under the staging cwd (initial build failed; earlier 200s that looked like success were actually the owners own stale 197 server on 8080 — process-tree check caught it). Fix: run_dev_entry passes its own current_exe() as JET_BIN; DevServer prefers JET_BIN over PATH. 196s dev() is now just devserver.app() + serve(). New test jet_dev_app_zero_arg_watches_launched_file (no PATH doctoring — proves JET_BIN/JET_DEV_FILE plumbing alone suffices). Verified end-to-end from a foreign cwd incl. rebuild-on-save. Full workspace + golden green.

Big pivot per owner: dev-server config moves from CLI flags/file-top markers into real Jet code. Built fn dev() as a well-known optional entry point (like main, no new syntax): jet dev <file> checks for it first; if present, compiles the file NATIVELY with dev() swapped in as the real entry (AST-level rename before codegen, reusing the same you-can-swap-entry idea as jet test/jet bench, not a new CompileMode), runs the resulting binary, and dev()s own Jet code configures+starts a real core.devserver value (devserver.for_app(file).html(...).port(...).serve()). The running compiled program cant link the compiler, so serve() shells out to jet build --target=web for every rebuild (subprocess, not a library call) -- new Prelude/DevServer.rs, std-only. If no fn dev() exists, falls straight through to todays default (jet dev --target=web / #Target(Web) inference), unchanged -- verified via the pre-existing test suite untouched.

Found + fixed a real ordering bug during my own verification (not caught by the automated test, which used a fixture without #Target(Web)): the #Target(Web)-inferred built-in server check ran BEFORE the fn dev() check, so any file with both markers -- e.g. 196, which already had #Target(Web) from earlier this session -- could never actually reach the new path; it silently fell back to the old built-in server every time, looking identical from the outside (same port, same content served). Reordered so fn dev() is checked first (more specific override wins). Verified for real this time by checking the process tree for the actual compiled child binary + confirming a live jet build subprocess-driven rebuild-on-save, not just that a server responded on the port.

fn build() (comptime/build procedure) intentionally NOT built -- overlaps unratified card #38, owner asked to scope separately.

Re-blessed one stale ui/ snapshot (core.devserver in E1001s known-module-list fix text). Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

1) Clone report: no actual bug. All *.clone() reaching JS were already fixed; the confusion was L0801 (a pre-existing lint) warning 3x per build on 197 for capturing Signal/Backend handles into reactive_render closures -- the idiomatic pattern every example this session uses. Flagged as possibly miscalibrated (cheap Rc-clone captures shouldnt need take()) but not changed without owner confirmation.

2) D-HTMLPAIR1 raised+built: #Html("path.html") file-level marker (same family as #Target(Web)), explicit instead of the silent <stem>.html convention; missing file is now a loud build error, not a silent fallback. New Program/LoadedModule.html_path AST field, WebArtifacts.explicit_html_path, precedence explicit-marker > sibling-convention > generic page.

3) #Js reorg attempt on 197: tried grouping via existing #Target(Js) module {} (cascades bucket to members, confirmed). Found 2 real bugs this exposed: struct declared inside inline module invisible to sibling fns (general E0119, no web involved), and moving a fn into a module changes native codegen enough to break struct-field-forward cloning (I2 rustc rejection). Both documented in 197s source, NOT fixed (routed around) -- reverted to the working per-fn #Js tags. Module-grouping is NOT safe to recommend yet.

4) Real regression caught+fixed during dogfooding: first cut of D-WEBDEFAULT1 inferred web for jet run too, which tried to exec a .wasm/.js bundle as a native binary and failed. jet run now never infers from marker/manifest (native-only, requires explicit --target=web); build/dev/check still infer. New regression test jet_cli_run_never_infers_web_target_from_marker.

196 and 197 now both carry explicit #Target(Web) + #Html(...) (dogfooded). 4 new tests total this round. Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Flagship showcase (197_ui_showcase.jet/.html): all 5 mechanisms wired together for real -- typed View tree (native-only cluster, printed), typed Color->hex (real integer-arithmetic conversion feeding ui.node_color, not a shortcut), component-kit-style composed functions (stat_card/paint_stat_card), Clock-driven tween motion (Fuel card, real requestAnimationFrame loop), two independent reactive.signal-driven cards (Boosts counter, Fuel elapsed-time), all painting real DOM elements. Found+fixed 3 more real JS-codegen gaps (StructLit construction, to_float/to_int, sema-inserted .clone() -- all were silently producing undefined, a real correctness hazard) plus a multi-node DOM-identity collision (scope-keyed element registry, was single global querySelector). New test web_showcase_dashboard_roundtrip.

Also shipped: --port=<N> flag on jet dev --target=web (explicit port fails loud, no silent fallback). And D-WEBDEFAULT1 (raised open in Tower, owner gave clear direction live in chat but formal ratification still pending): #Target(Web) file-level marker + pkg.jet target:"web" field, so jet run/dev/build infer the web backend without --target=web every time; CLI flag still overrides both. New Program.default_target AST field, PackageMeta.target manifest field, effective_target()/manifest_default_target() helpers in main.rs. 2 new integration tests + 1 new ui/ snapshot (E0003 on #Target(Web) module, invalid position). Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Phase 7 extension continued (owner feedback): (1) visual polish on 196_ui_web_click.html (dark-mode card layout, gradient background, real button styling) and the generic auto-emitted index.html (both now genuinely presentable, not bare unstyled boxes). (2) Real jet dev <file> --target=web command (Source/CmdDevWeb.rs, new): std-only (I6) TCP static file server + mtime-poll rebuild-on-save (reuses file_mtime from run_dev) + browser live-reload via polled /__jet_dev_version + location.reload(), so viewing/iterating on a Jet web app needs zero Node/npm. Factored CmdCompile::build webs write step into shared write_web_artifacts(file, web, verbose, out_dir) so build and dev share one path (I8). New test tests/web_dev.rs (spawns the real jet binary, confirms serve + real rebuild-on-edit, 5/5 stable runs). Found + fixed a real intermittent rename-race in the staging-swap (fs::rename occasionally saw a not-yet-visible file under concurrent load) with a bounded retry — reproducible only under heavy concurrent nix develop load in this sandbox, not clearly a real-machine issue, but the retry is cheap and correct either way. tools/web-serve.mjs (the earlier Node workaround) is now superseded — kept for now, not deleted, since it still works standalone. Full cargo test --workspace + golden green after a stray /tmp nix-shell buildup was cleared (unrelated env issue, not a regression).

Phase 3/7 wiring closed the color gap flagged earlier: JetUiNode gained a real color field, ui.node_color(label,w,h,color_hex) constructor (mirrors node_role), both native backends paint() now use node.color (falls back to #000000, same default as before) instead of a hardcoded literal, and DomRuntime.js real-DOM paint() sets the actual background + a WCAG-luminance-picked readable text color. Also fixed a real JS-codegen gap hit while wiring this: Stmt::Assign (plain local reassignment, LValue::Local, S17 compound ops) was silently dropped by emit_js_body — any `x = expr`/`x += expr` inside an #Js fn body vanished with no error. Now emitted correctly; documented as still LValue::Local only (index/field assignment still unsupported, consistent with the phases narrow-scope note). examples/features/196_ui_web_click.jet now uses ui.node_color with a real color that changes every 5th click, verified end-to-end via the fake-DOM test harness (background/color asserted, not just position/text). Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Phase 7 extension (post-close, at owner request): made the web/DOM backend actually viewable in a real browser, not just a node-run command log. DomRuntime.js paint()/createBackend() now mount real DOM elements under #jet-app when a document exists (no-op under node, existing snapshot tests untouched); every top-level #Js fn is now exported (not just main) so a hand-authored host page can call one directly (e.g. a button onclick); jet build --target=web now also emits build/index.html (generic jet_main()-only loader by default, or a sibling <stem>.html next to the .jet source if one exists). New example 196_ui_web_click.jet + examples/features/196_ui_web_click.html (real click-counter, click increments a live DOM element) + tools/web-serve.mjs (dependency-free static server for build/, since ES module imports need real http:// not file://). New test web_click_counter_dom_roundtrip in tests/web_build.rs (fake-DOM harness, no new npm dep) proves the element is created once and reused across renders, not duplicated. Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Phases 1-7 done and verified (view tree, typed styles, component kit, motion, a11y, web backend). Phase 8 (native backends) blocked: the plan text says platform-gated with #Target(os), but #Target today ONLY means the D-WASM1 web-target marker (Browser/Wasm/Js) — there is no ratified syntax for gating a module/impl to a native OS (Linux/macOS/Windows). Raised D-OSTARGET1 (3 options: extend #Target with Os.* variants / new dedicated #Os marker / manifest-level gating in pkg.jet, rec=A) rather than inventing syntax. Separately, this sandbox has no GTK/AppKit/Win32 dev headers or pkg-config available (verified) — even once D-OSTARGET1 is ratified, a real linked native backend cannot be built/tested here without a flake/devShell change to add platform toolkit dependencies, which is its own decision the owner should see before its assumed. Card stays in deciding for Phase 8 only; do not close c134 until D-OSTARGET1 is ratified and a native backend actually builds+runs behind it.

Phase 7 done: web/DOM backend. Codegen/Web.rs gained lambda emission + reactive.signal -> jetDom.makeSignal + ui.reactive_render dispatch; DomRuntime.js gained a dependency-tracked reactive shim mirroring Rust JetSignal (still in-memory command log, no real document API — no browser under node, by design). New web_reactive_dom_snapshot_roundtrip test in tests/web_build.rs actually runs the emitted JS via node and diffs stdout against a fixture (the web DOM snapshot). Example 195_ui_web_reactive.jet runs identically native + web (both expected outputs verified). JS codegen scope intentionally narrow (documented list of supported constructs). Verified myself: cargo build clean, web_build 6/6 green, native jet run correct output. Flagged not fixed: D-JSBIND1 referenced as ratified in code comments but has no standalone row in syntax-decisions.md.

Phase 6 done: a11y. JetAriaRole (Button/TextInput/Label/Container) + JetUiNode.role + keyboard focus routing (Tab cycles a focus-group list) in Prelude/Ui.rs; new ui.node_role/aria_role_* constructors (existing ui.node untouched, no golden regressions). E2930 (empty accessible label on interactive node) + E2931 (duplicate label across focus-group) as Severity::Lint diagnostics, filtered out of build/run/check/emit output and only surfaced via new jet lint --a11y <file> CLI subcommand (Source/CLI.rs, main.rs, CmdDevTools.rs) — verified jet run/build on the same problem files succeed with zero a11y output (D-A11YGATE1=B non-blocking requirement held). Both checks are static/literal-only by design (documented scope, not a heuristic). Example 194_ui_a11y.jet + 2 tests/ui_lint snapshots, all verified by hand + targeted test runs (golden, cli, lint_snapshots, ui_backend, decisions, ui, jet-sema --lib all green).

Phase 5 done: motion. Plain user-space tween() (smoothstep ease, clamped) over the already-real injectable Clock (core.time.clock) + reactive.signal/derived — motion value is a pure Computed<T> of elapsed clock time, never imperatively .set(). No new compiler machinery, no new bugs hit. Example 193_ui_motion.jet, golden-tested with exact binary-fraction outputs (byte-exact, no float flakiness).

Phase 4 done: ownable component kit. jetpack add <Name> (Button/Label/Input/Container, exact-case catalog match) copies embedded .jet source into components/ in the user project (Jetpack/Components.rs, include_str!-embedded from Jetpack/components/*.jet); refuses to clobber an already-owned file. Existing jetpack add <source>:<pkg> package-ref path unaffected (verified). Example 192_ui_component_kit.jet composes all four over one View tree, golden-tested. 3 unit tests + full e2e binary run verified. Found + documented 2 more real compiler bugs (not fixed, routed around): (1) I2 ICE — forwarding an unmodified fn param into an enum dot-variant field moves out of a shared ref instead of cloning (E0507); (2) sema gap — list-literal element position does not get dot-variant type inference that struct-field position gets, and E0330s own suggested EnumName.Variant.{} fallback does not parse either.

Phase 3 done: typed Style (flat record per D-STYLESHAPE1) + Color + Length/LengthUnit as plain user-space Jet struct/enum (same recipe as Phase 2 View, zero new core-type registration). No backend wiring into JetPaintCmd since color:String there is not yet settable from Jet source (nothing load-bearing to wire into). No new diagnostics — construction errors already covered by generic E0303. Found + documented (not fixed, out of scope) a real TIR-subset-coverage bug: a struct field of a distinct/#UnitFamily type ICEs codegen (worked around using flat struct+enum Length instead of #UnitFamily sugar). Example examples/features/191_ui_typed_style.jet, golden-tested.

Phase 1 done: computed alias fix + 3 pre-existing test-compile breaks fixed (Reflect.rs Span import, TIR/mod.rs ProgramBundle missing fields, 2 stale-syntax unit tests, jet-driver fixture path) — cargo test --workspace now fully green (was broken on master before this card). Phase 2 done: named-payload enum variants (S30, VariantPayload::Named) now construct via .Variant.{ field: val } / Type.Variant.{ field: val } per D-UITREE1s ratified spelling — this was previously UNIMPLEMENTED (EnumLitArg::Named was dead code in the parser despite full sema/codegen/formatter support). Added parser production (enum_lit_named_fields), fixed a codegen pattern-match bug (positional variant patterns fabricated f0/f1 instead of real field names for Named payloads), fixed a P0 sema infinite-recursion bug (is_cloneable had no cycle guard, so ANY self-referential type crashed the compiler with a stack overflow the moment it flowed through a reactive.derived/effect/computed closure capture check). View tree + diff-based rerender demonstrated in examples/features/190_ui_view_tree.jet (golden-tested), fmt round-trip test added, ui snapshot added for the new E0303 fix-text. Full cargo test --workspace green. Remaining: Phase 3 typed styles, Phase 4 component kit, Phase 5 motion, Phase 6 a11y, Phase 7 web backend completion, Phase 8 native backend.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: package hash fields — canonical Store v2 owned by #393
cards.body: Historical model recorded hashes/paths but is not an immutable canonical content store. No CAS capability claim remains on this card.
cards.plan: D-CASTORE1=A: extend build-cache hashing to cover package identity. Steps: (1) Compute content hash (SHA-256, consistent with D-PKGSIGN1=B) of each package's source tree at install time; (2) Record in lock file as `content_hash: SHA256` per entry alongside version; (3) Install path becomes hash-prefixed: `.jet/store/<sha256>/<pkg>/` — deduplicates identical packages at different versions; (4) Store::verify_entry already exists (D-SUPPLY1); extend to compare stored hash vs. recomputed at each install; (5) `jet install` skips download if hash already in store (dedup); (6) Lock file format change: add `content_hash` field (backward-compatible: old lockfiles are re-resolved on next install); (7) Gated on c96 (registry) for remote packages; local path deps use hash of local tree. No new user-facing syntax. Tests in tests/ui/.

log.text: 2026-07-09 truth audit: reclassified from shipped capability to historical substrate; world-class milestone owns live completion.

D-CASTORE1=A ratified. Proceed: extend build-cache hashing to cover package identity. Lock file records content hash; install path is hash-prefixed. Dedup, tamper detection, future signed cache. Changes lock file format.
Plan written. Extension of existing store/lock infrastructure. Advancing to ready.

Implemented. LockedPackage.content_hash: Option<String> added to Lock.rs schema (backward-compatible: old lockfiles parse as None). cards.title: Legacy substrate: age-based hangar cleanup — closure-safe GC owned by #393/#420
cards.body: Historical cleanup scans nearest project state and lacks global closure roots/leases. It is not the production GC contract.
cards.plan:
U22 plan: hangar disk contract

Decision: D-JPK-GC1=B plus owner amendment is ratified. Verb is jet clean, not jet gc. Default stale_after is 30 days. Auto-GC is opportunistic and no-daemon. jet clean does GC plus optimize/dedup. Lockfile and generation reachable objects are never collected. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add reachability scan in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs from .jet/lock package/toolchain entries and future jetos generation roots. Treat unknown legacy records as live until proven stale.
2. Extend hangar meta.json written by Store::record with last_used/realized timestamps and preserve envelope/source-state fields. Refresh last_used on cache reuse.
3. Replace current blunt Store::clean, which removes every entry. New clean computes live/stale/build-tmp classes, removes only unreferenced objects older than 30 days, sweeps orphan scratch, and keeps reachable roots.
4. Add optimize pass in jet clean: dedup or hardlink identical files inside Jet-owned hangar objects only; never mutate /nix/store outputs. Report GC bytes and optimize bytes separately.
5. Route build scratch under hangar tmp in Provider.rs / Recipe.rs / Store.rs. Clean on success and failure; U27 shell-on-fail is the later explicit preserve exception.
6. Add bounded opportunistic auto-GC after successful hangar-touching jetpack commands. No daemon, no root.
7. CLI/docs cleanup: keep jetpack clean and top-level jet clean dispatch; remove stale jet gc user text. Fix E2604 fix text in docs/spec/diagnostics.md and Source/Publish/Advisory.rs from jet gc --force to jet clean.

Likely touched: crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs, CLI.rs, Provider.rs, Recipe.rs, Lock.rs, WorkspaceLock.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, Source/main.rs, EngineDispatch.rs, Source/Publish/Advisory.rs, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/roadmap.md, tests/jetpack.rs, tests/pkg.rs, CLI transcript snapshots.

Diagnostics/tests/docs: no new diagnostic unless corrupt metadata or permission handling needs a stable code. Must update E2604 docs/fix text and any snapshot mentioning jet gc. Document 30d stale_after, live/stale/build-tmp classes, and zero-/tmp contract.

Targeted tests: old unreferenced object removed after 30d; 29d kept; lock-reachable kept regardless of age; legacy malformed metadata kept conservatively; orphan hangar tmp swept; active tmp marker kept; identical owned files dedup and report saved bytes; jetpack clean leaves live package runnable; zero-/tmp build/crash golden; jet hangar du matches on-disk bytes.

Gates: Store::clean never deletes reachable packages; no writes outside hangar/.jet in tested build paths; jet clean is only public GC verb; targeted tests then full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace green in implementation session.

cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-PLATFORM1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one canonical platform model for jetpack targets: linux, macos, windows plus arch keys used by the hangar envelope. Keep jetos Linux-only and keep Nix bridge Linux/macOS-only.
2. Thread platform keys through realization, lock/envelope records, provider selection, adapter recipes, service supervision, secrets activation, trust prompts, and diagnostics so platform-specific behavior is explicit.
3. Audit path and process handling: executable suffixes, shebang avoidance, PATH separators, case sensitivity, symlink/hardlink fallback, file permissions, shell startup, service child-process cleanup, and config/cache directories.
4. Stand up CI matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Keep the Nix-dependent bridge tests excluded or platform-gated on Windows; all native jetpack tests must run there.
5. Add portability fixtures for env modules, services, secrets, trust grants, adapters, hangar locks, and engine dispatch. Make every platform skip explicit and tied to D-JPK-PLATFORM1, not ad hoc.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Envelope,Store,Provider,Recipe,RefSpec,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI}.rs`

cards.title: Legacy substrate: no-daemon policy/status — enforced sandbox owned by #398
cards.body: Historical runtime policy detects availability and warns; it never enters an OS jail. No strong-sandbox claim remains.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-NODAEMON1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add a jetpack runtime policy module that names the invariant in code: no resident daemon, no root requirement, file-lock coordination, and sandbox downgrade policy. Keep jetos activation as the only future sudo exception.
2. Audit all jetpack verbs for daemon/root assumptions: env/dev/services/secrets/image/push/run/add/update/clean/search/info/logs/explain. Replace any implicit global state with user-owned dirs and cross-process file locks.
3. Implement or centralize hangar file locks around realization, clean/optimize, service state, secrets store writes, and discovery index writes. Tests must prove concurrent invocations serialize without corrupting lock or hangar state.
4. Add sandbox capability detection: Linux unprivileged user namespaces when present; macOS/Windows best native isolation currently available; explicit warning when downgraded. Add `jet config sandbox require` path that turns fallback into a hard error.
5. Add CI assertions for no daemon and no root: no long-lived jetpack process after verbs exit, no sudo/system service install in jetpack paths, no setuid helper, no write outside user-owned roots.
6. Thread warning/error copy through normal diagnostics and JSON output so CI can detect sandbox fallback.

Likely touched files/modules:
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/RuntimePolicy.rs`, `Sandbox.rs`, or `Locking.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Store,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI,Provider,Recipe,WorkspaceLock}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`; platform CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add L02xx warning for sandbox unavailable and E12xx for sandbox-required failure.
- Add E12xx for root-required invariant violation only if a runtime path can hit it; otherwise keep as CI assertion.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, CLI help for `jet config sandbox require`, and epoch-4 docs.
- Ensure `--json` carries sandbox status without ANSI or prose scraping.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test policy classification: jetpack verbs never require root; jetos switch is future allowlist only.
2. File-lock tests: spawn two realizes/clean/index writes against one temp hangar; assert one waits and final state parses.
3. Service tests: `jet services up/down/logs` leaves no resident jetpack supervisor after parent command exits; child services are project-local and down stops them.
4. Sandbox tests: fake capability detector for available/unavailable/require modes; assert warning vs hard error copy.
5. Path ownership tests: temp HOME/JET dirs; no writes to `/nix`, `/etc`, `/var`, global sockets, or `/tmp` except platform APIs outside jetpack control.
6. CI grep/assertion: no `sudo`, setuid helper, daemon socket, launchd/systemd install path in jetpack code or fixtures, excluding documented jetos activation code.

Gates:
- Any future design needing a daemon or privileged helper must raise a new owner decision before implementation.
- Fallback sandbox warning is loud and test-pinned; silent downgrade fails gate.
- Cross-platform behavior matches U25.
- Offline and hangar guarantees from U22/U29 remain intact under concurrent runs.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: fixture offline sweep — syscall/closure proof owned by #395/#433
cards.body: Historical offline fixture reuses fabricated provider output; it does not prove verified closure substitution or OS-level network denial.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-OFFLINE1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one `NetworkMode` or `OfflineMode` value threaded through jetpack CLI dispatch, resolver, providers, adapters, cache substitution, script deps, service startup, and build runner. `--offline` must be parsed once and passed explicitly.
2. Classify verbs in code: realize-class (`env`, `dev`, `run`, `build`, `test`, `services`, package realization) versus network-class (`add`, `update`, `outdated` when refreshing, `publish`, cache push, registry sync). Network-class verbs refuse under `--offline` before doing work.
3. Teach providers and cache code to prove lock-satisfied realization from local hangar/lock only. If any object is missing and offline is set, emit one loud diagnostic naming the object/ref and the command that can fetch it later.
4. Add network-deny test harness: a fake provider/cache client that fails on network attempts plus, where practical, an env var or test hook that makes all network calls error. Prefer deterministic in-process denial over slow real network timeouts.
5. Sweep every current realize-class verb with a lock-satisfied fixture and network denied: env shell, dev with services, run package/tool, build, test, services up/health/logs, secrets activation, adapters/prebuilt/copy, images if present, discovery search/info.
6. Update docs/diagnostics and CLI help. Make `--offline` visible in completions/man output and stable JSON errors.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{CLI,Provider,RefSpec,Store,Recipe,ScriptDeps,ScriptLock,Services,Secrets,Trust,Image,Discovery}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Fetch,Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,CLISpec,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,cli}.rs`; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E1258 or next free E12xx for offline-forbids-network and reuse it for fetch misses and network-class refusal, with specific What/Why/Fix per context.
- Add diagnostics.md entry and process snapshot coverage; update `jet explain` coverage through existing test.
- Document verb classification in epoch-4 docs and user CLI help.
- Ensure no ANSI, spinner, or timeout text in offline errors.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test verb classification and `--offline` flag parsing through engine dispatch.
2. Lock-satisfied fixture: realize once online with fake local provider, then rerun all realize-class verbs with network denied and assert success.
3. Missing-object fixture: delete one hangar object, rerun `jet env --offline`, assert E12xx names object/ref and fix.
4. Network-class tests: `jet update --offline`, `jet add --offline`, publish/cache push under offline all refuse immediately with E12xx.
5. Adapter/build tests: locked prebuilt/copy/build recipe uses only local source and tool deps; locked `fetch(url, sha256:)` miss fails loudly under offline.
6. Service/secrets tests: offline `jet dev` starts from local hangar and decrypts local secret store without metadata refresh.
7. Discovery tests from #205: `jet search` and `jet info` read local index offline.

Gates:
- No network from realize-class verbs when lock is satisfied.
- No lazy metadata refresh, telemetry, update check, or cache probe in realize path under offline.
- Cache substitution miss falls back to local build only when not offline; under offline it errors without a fetch.
- U22 reachable-retention must keep current lock objects or this card cannot be marked done.
- Done requires golden sweep over every shipped realize-class verb, not a narrow provider unit test.

cards.title: LSP v2 — professional editor engine
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: jet lsp serves hover/defn/refs/rename/completion/semantic-tokens/inlay/fmt/code-actions — but full-document sync (re-sends whole file per keystroke), no outline (documentSymbol), no workspace symbols, no signature help, no folding, no occurrences highlight, no call hierarchy, no snippets. Owner: 'LSP seems substantially insufficient.' Two decisions: engine architecture (D-LSP1) and capability bar (D-LSP2).
cards.plan:
LSP v2 under D-LSP1=C (one incremental compiler service) + D-LSP2=A (full LSP 3.17 parity, beginner-first order). Implement on master (this plan was authored from the stale tower-platform worktree; all paths verified against master). Invariants: I2 front end owns every message, I3 checking lives in sema, I6 zero external crates in the compiler — the query engine is std-only.

Architecture (D-LSP1=C): a demand-driven incremental query engine — inputs (file text, module graph roots) and derived queries (tokens-of-file, ast-of-file, module-graph, types-of-item, diagnostics-of-file, symbols-of-file, callers-of-item), each memoized with precise dependency tracking and a global revision counter. jet check, jet dev, the REPL, and jet lsp become clients of the same engine, so editor answers can never disagree with the compiler. jet-semindex's ratified query API (D-SEMINDEX1) is the persistence/format layer, fed by the engine instead of batch runs.

Build order:
1. Engine core: new crate crates/jet-queries (std-only). Query trait + memo table + dependency edges + revision invalidation. Wrap existing lexer/parser/sema entry points as queries without changing their internals (I3). Unit tests: edit one file of a 3-file project, prove only dependent queries recompute (counter assertions).
2. LSP on the engine: rewrite Source/LSP/Check.rs request paths to engine queries; keep the JSON/protocol layer. Differential gate: LSP publishDiagnostics byte-identical to `jet check --json` for every tests/ui fixture (new tests/lsp differential test — this is the no-two-brains exit).
3. Incremental sync: textDocumentSync 2 (range edits) in Server.rs + rope-or-line-table doc storage in Position.rs. Latency test: single-keystroke edit on a 2,000-line fixture re-checks in <10ms warm (test with counters, not wall-clock flake; a wall-clock smoke stays #[ignore] for local runs).
4. Wave 1 — beginner-critical (ships before anything else user-visible): signatureHelp (trigger '(' and ','; params + doc comment from AST), documentSymbol (nested outline: fns, structs+methods, enums, traits, modules), completion quality pass (labels get type signatures; keyword completions context-filtered).
5. Wave 2 — navigation: workspaceSymbol (engine project view), foldingRange (blocks, comments, use-groups), documentHighlight (occurrences via resolution, read vs write kinds — v5 & writes light differently), selectionRange (AST-walk expand).
6. Wave 3 — power: completion auto-import (insert `use` on commit) + snippet support (fn call parens, .{ } constructor), prepareRename (reject keywords/foreign symbols with Jet-voiced message), semanticTokens range + delta (keep full as fallback), inlayHint refinements (param names at call sites, off-by-default toggle).
7. Wave 4 — hierarchy + long tail: callHierarchy (incoming/outgoing via callers-of-item query), typeHierarchy (impl/trait relations), documentLink (use-paths + doc URLs), codeLens (run/test lens over #Test fns, off by default). Advertise only what ships: initialize_response in Server.rs grows per wave, never ahead of tests.
8. Engine serves the CLI: `jet check` and `jet dev` reuse the warm engine in watch/daemon mode (D-DEV4 loop); differential battery from E2-M4 must stay green (interpreter parity untouched).

Exit criteria (all must hold — no partial done):
- Every capability advertised in initialize_response has a passing test in tests/lsp.rs (capability-coverage meta-test enumerates the JSON and fails on untested ones).
- Differential gate (stage 2) green across all ui fixtures.
- Incremental-recompute unit proofs green; keystroke path does not re-run whole-file sema when edit is local to one item.
- tests/lsp/, tests/dev.rs, tests/repl.rs, full suite green.
- docs: editors/vscode/README.md + editors/zed/README.md feature tables updated; architecture.md gains the query-engine section (R-rules untouched).

Gates: none open — D-LSP1/D-LSP2 ratified 2026-07-05. Log both in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md tooling section during stage 1 commit.

Delegation: stages 1–3 sequential (one agent, non-isolated — worktree agents branch stale bases); waves 4–7 parallelizable per-feature after stage 3 lands. sonnet for feature waves, opus for stage 1 engine design review before code.

cards.title: CI and quality gates — the professional bar
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: CI runs 5 of ~70 test targets (lib, truthfulness, diagnostic_snapshots, golden, cross) — lsp, fmt, repl, jetpack, workspace, web_build, ownership etc. never run on PR. CI also still calls frozen tools/Tower/Tower.mjs (MOVED.md says don't). No clippy/rustfmt/warning gate; no perf-regression or fuzz cadence. Decisions: D-CI1 gate composition, D-CI2 warning policy.
cards.plan:
CI + quality gates under D-CI1=A (full suite sharded on every PR; nightly perf/fuzz/coverage/multi-OS) and D-CI2=A (zero-warning gate with card-referenced #[expect]). Implement on master.

Build order:
1. Warning sweep first (D-CI2): fix or #[expect(lint, reason = "#<card>: <why>")] every current warning across the workspace. Known: scrutinee_bool in crates/jet-jit/src/lib.rs:1916 gets #[expect(dead_code, reason = "#125: JIT tier-1a scrutinee lowering, wired in next stage")]. Rule goes in CLAUDE.md style section: dead code without a card-referenced expect is deletable on sight; expects self-expire (unfulfilled-expectation errors when the code goes live).
2. Lint config: [workspace.lints] in root Cargo.toml — rust.warnings = deny in CI (via RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings in the workflow, not in the manifest, so local iteration stays friendly); clippy correctness+suspicious groups on, style/pedantic off (house conventions win). rustfmt.toml matching current formatting (verify `cargo fmt --check` is near-clean first; if a one-time format commit is needed it is its own mechanical commit, no logic changes).
3. Shard the suite: 4 PR jobs with an explicit shard map (a checked-in list, e.g. tools/ci/shards.toml): shard-1 front-end (lexer/parser/fmt/grammar/ui/ui_lint/syntax_reconciliation...), shard-2 sema (ownership/generics/effects/typestate/pure/taint...), shard-3 codegen+examples (golden/canon/cross/corelib/release_gates...), shard-4 tooling (lsp/repl/debug/dev/jetpack/pkg/workspace/web_*/observe/cli...). Meta-test tools/ci/shards-complete (or tests/ci_shards.rs): every tests/*.rs file assigned to exactly one shard, fails on unassigned new files — no silent coverage loss, ever.
4. Rewrite .github/workflows/ci.yml: keep nix toolchain job skeleton; PR = build + 4 shard jobs (nix develop -c cargo test --test <list>) + cargo fmt --check + clippy + tower status via NEW path (node Tower/tower.mjs status — the frozen tools/Tower/Tower.mjs step dies) + aarch64 QEMU smoke as today. Cache /nix and cargo target dir keyed on flake.lock+Cargo.lock so shard wall-clock stays near today's.
5. Nightly workflow (.github/workflows/nightly.yml): full suite on ubuntu + macos; perf ratchet via tools/perf/ci-perf-check.sh against tools/perf/baseline.json (regression = red + auto card via tower CLI); fuzz cadence — run tests/fuzz_sema.rs in extended mode (env-gated iteration count) 30 min; coverage report (nix devshell tool; CI-side only, not a compiler dep — I6 untouched) published as artifact with a ratchet floor once a baseline exists.
6. Failure→card automation: nightly failure step runs `node Tower/tower.mjs card add --kind bug ...` with the failing job link (guard against duplicates by title search first).
7. Canary proof: after everything lands, a deliberate throwaway PR breaking a previously-unrun target (e.g. tests/repl.rs) must go red; record the run link on this card, then close the canary.

Exit criteria:
- PR CI executes every tests/*.rs target (shard meta-test green and enforced).
- cargo build clean under -Dwarnings on Linux+macOS; every expect carries a card reference.
- Frozen tools/Tower path gone from CI; new tower status step green.
- Nightly runs green end-to-end once; perf ratchet demonstrably fails on an injected slowdown (test the tester, then revert).
- Canary PR proof recorded.

Gates: none — D-CI1/D-CI2 ratified 2026-07-05. Note: grammar-drift step from #210 joins the PR gate when #210 lands; leave a commented step referencing #210.

Delegation: stage 1 sweep is mechanical (haiku/sonnet); stages 3–5 one sonnet agent (single-file workflow edits test poorly in parallel); verify by running the shard lists locally once (nix develop -c cargo test --test <shard list>) before pushing.

cards.title: Bootstrap readiness gate: dogfood portfolio + memory-model soundness campaign
cards.body:
HARD GATE for e8 — no port work starts until this card is done and owner signs off. Core lang must be locked-happy (stdlib may still flux).

Evidence required:
1. **Dogfood portfolio** — enough real example projects in Jet, chosen for fringe needs and complexity, to stress the language end-to-end: compiler-shaped programs (formatter port, interpreter, arena/index-handle AST work), long-lived concurrent services, comptime-heavy code, FFI-heavy code, large multi-package workspaces. Each project reviewed for (a) readability and (b) how well an agent/human can reason about the codebase cold.
2. **Memory-model soundness campaign** — adversarial stress of memory model v5 (D-MEM1: bare/read, &/write, ^/take, second-class borrows) to Rust-borrow-checker confidence: soundness test suite, fuzzing, differential testing vs rustc on generated code, deliberate escape attempts (use-after-take, aliasing writes, arena dangling-index patterns), and I1 audit that no safe-Jet program can reach UB. Exit = virtually 100% certainty it is as solid as Rust.
3. **Syntax/coverage sweep** — every ratified surface feature exercised in the portfolio; gaps become examples or ballots.
4. **Owner sign-off ballot** — final "core lang is frozen enough to port" decision, minted when evidence is assembled.

Blocks the full-port card.

cards.title: Full port: self-host the Jet compiler in Jet
cards.body:
Tracks the entire bootstrap arc. Gated by the readiness card (blockedBy) — do not start before it is done and owner-signed.

Owner gates to mint as ballots when e8 opens:
- **D-SELFHOST1 charter** — port scope: (A) rewrite in Jet, keep emitting Rust + hidden rustc backend; (B) native backend first, rustc leaves the bootstrap chain; (C) piecewise, one crate at a time via C-ABI linking into the Rust driver.
- **I6 restatement** — zero-external-deps invariant re-expressed for Jet compiler source + what stage0 may be (pinned Rust-built release binary).
- **I2 fate** — if the Jet compiler still emits Rust, bootstrap forever needs a Rust toolchain; owner accepts or demands the native backend first.

Mechanics:
- Stage discipline: stage0 = pinned Rust-built jet; stage1 = jet compiled by stage0; stage2 = jet compiled by stage1; exit test = stage1 ≡ stage2 byte-identical. Requires deterministic codegen (no hash-order leaks, no timestamps).
- Feature-freeze line: self-hosted compiler uses only the Jet subset stage0 supports; lint against drift.
- Test-harness parity: golden tests, tests/ui snapshots, tests/decisions.rs run unchanged against the Jet-built binary.
- Subsystem inventory to scope per-ballot: lexer, parser, sema (incl. memory model v5 checker), codegen, comptime tier-0 interpreter, JIT tier (see #10/#11 — Cranelift cannot port; own VM/JIT cards own that), jet fmt, LSP, jet debug, jetpack driver. Some may stay Rust indefinitely — charter decides.
- Cheapest credible first step once unblocked: port the lexer, link into the Rust driver via C ABI, run the full suite — generates the real gap list.

cards.title: Build functional jetos Studio prototype
cards.body: Owner acceptance: jetos Studio must be a usable source-backed GUI, not only a plan. Implement the ratified `jetos studio` surface as a first prototype over canonical Jet modules: load a project, select host, render guided control panels plus source/diff/provenance, edit real settings through source transactions, show plan/proof/rollback status, and refuse hidden GUI-owned semantic state. Done means a user can edit a jetos config in Studio, preview the exact Jet diff, save, reproject, and run the corresponding jetos check/build/proof flow.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.process — subprocess parity with Python subprocess/Go os/exec
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python subprocess flexibility, Go os/exec explicitness, duct-style pipelines. Current: run([cmd]) capturing everything + exit(code) only.

Gaps: streaming stdin write and incremental stdout/stderr read while the child runs; env control (set, remove, clear-then-set); working-directory control; timeout with kill; send signals (terminate/kill/interrupt); detached spawn; exit status detail (signal vs code); pipelines (child stdout → child stdin) without a shell; safe argv-only execution documented (no shell interpolation footgun — safe by default); output size limits; inherit-vs-capture per stream.

Done means: a build-tool-shaped example (spawn, stream logs live, timeout, propagate exit) ships with golden output. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan:
Acceptance: core.process must cover real build-tool and agent-operation workflows without shell strings: safe argv-only execution by default, streaming logs, exact exit status, env/cwd control, timeouts, signals, detached children, output limits, and shell-free pipelines.

Current facts found during plan pass:
- docs/reference/core-library.md documents only process.exit(code) and process.run([String]) -> ProcessResult ? IOError.
- ProcessResult currently has code/output/errors only.
- Sema/codegen know core.process exit/run only; effects classify core.process as Exec.
- Existing taint tests treat process.run as an Exec sink; any expanded surface must keep that policy coverage.

Gate queued:
- D-PROCESS1: exact process spawning/pipeline surface.

Implementation plan after gate clears:
1. Baseline tests: pin current process.run/exit behavior and taint Exec-sink coverage before expanding.
2. Data model: add ProcessSpec, Child, ExitStatus, StreamMode, ProcessPipe/Pipeline types per ratified surface. Keep argv lists canonical; no shell-string helper unless separately ratified.
3. Sema/effects: register all new calls in CheckerCoreLib known-items, mark Exec effects, preserve taint sink checks on every execution path, and type-check stream/stdin/stdout modes.
4. Runtime/codegen: implement through TIR/prelude only; no codegen checks. Use std::process Command internally; map OS errors into IOError and child outcomes into ExitStatus without exposing Rust/stdout internals.
5. Safety defaults: bounded capture default or explicit output_limit, no inherited env mutation, timeout kill semantics documented, process handles RAII-clean where possible, and interrupt/terminate/kill behavior platform-pinned.
6. Examples/goldens: build_runner.jet streams stdout, sets cwd/env, times out a child, pipelines two argv commands, propagates exit. Keep fixture commands cross-platform or test-gated.
7. Docs: update docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/spec.md effects table, syntax-decisions D-PROCESS1 entry, and stdlib ledger (#310 if present).
8. Verification: targeted process/taint/golden tests, cargo build, hello smoke, process example smoke, final nix develop -c cargo test before close.

Devil-pass hardening:
- No shell string default; argv-only is the safe path.
- No silent output buffering footgun; streaming and capture limits are explicit.
- No second process model; process.run lowers to ProcessSpec.run.
- No raw OS status leaks; ExitStatus is typed and portable.
